Who we serve

Wholesale drinkware and barware for promotional product distributors

You buy against a client's campaign date, not a stock position. What you need from a factory is a fixed decoration cost, a proof that matches the artwork, and a ship date you can put in writing. That is the whole relationship.

Request a quoteBrowse the catalogue

What usually goes wrong

The five problems we hear most from this buyer type.

  • Decoration quoted late, after the client has already agreed a price
  • Proofs that do not match the finished print
  • Colour drift between the sample and the production run
  • Missing UPC or retail packaging that blocks the retail channel
  • A ship date that moves after the campaign is locked

What we take off your plate

Every quotation we issue for a distributor carries the decoration cost as a line item: print method, number of colours, setup, MOQ and lead time for the decorated version specifically. You get the number you need to price the campaign on day one, not after the order is placed.

Artwork goes through a virtual proof, and where the client needs it, a physical pre-production sample. Nothing goes into production until you approve the sample in writing. For colour-matched drinkware we issue a Pantone chip so the client signs off on the colour, not on a description of it.

Built for the way distributors actually buy

Most campaigns mix categories: a branded flute for the toast, a stopper or pourer as a giveaway, an ice bucket for the VIP table. Ordering those from three suppliers means three freight costs and three chances of a late shipment. We consolidate all of it into one order, one bill of lading and one entry, which also reduces the per-shipment customs processing fee.

Because the moulds are ours, we can hold the same rim thickness and base weight across seasons. When a client reorders the same item for next year's event, the glass looks the same, which is what keeps the account with you.

Packaging that works in both channels

The same item can ship as a plain export carton for a corporate giveaway, or as a printed colour box with a hang tag and a UPC barcode for retail shelf or an e-commerce listing. Tell us the channel at quotation stage and we will build the packaging into the unit cost rather than treating it as an afterthought.

Talk to us about your programme

Send the item list, quantities, decoration and destination. We reply with pricing by volume tier, lead time and carton data.

Wholesale drinkware and barware for promotional product distributors — questions

What is the printing minimum order for logo drinkware?

The minimum for each decoration method is confirmed per SKU and per decoration method in the quotation.

Do you provide virtual proofs and samples?

Yes. We return a virtual proof for layout approval, and a physical pre-production sample where the client needs to see the colour and finish. Samples are credited against the first bulk order.

Can you match a Pantone colour?

Yes. Send the Pantone reference and we will return a colour chip or a moulded sample for approval before production.

Can you supply UPC barcodes and retail packaging?

Yes. UPC barcodes, colour boxes, hang tags and shrink wrapping are all available. Tell us the retail channel at quotation stage so packaging is priced into the unit cost.

How do you handle a mixed-category campaign?

We consolidate all items into a single shipment and a single entry, which reduces freight and customs processing fees compared with splitting the order across suppliers.

What do you need from a distributor to quote a decorated order?

Send the SKU, the quantity, the logo artwork, the intended logo position, the decoration requirement, the packaging configuration and the in-hands date. Decoration is quoted as a separate line so you can see what the print itself costs.

Logo decoration guide

How do you handle a programme that reorders every year?

The approved SKU, artwork, decoration method, colour and packaging configuration are recorded with the order documentation, so a reorder is placed against the same approved brief instead of a new interpretation of it.
